title: Course Schedule
summary: Courses are nodes and prerequisites are edges; you can finish them all only if the graph has no cycle. Kahn's algorithm repeatedly takes a course with no remaining prerequisites. If every course gets taken, there's no cycle.

complexity.note: Each course and prerequisite is processed once.

intuition: In-degree = number of unfinished prerequisites.
Start with every course whose in-degree is 0.
Taking a course lowers its dependants' in-degrees; any that hit 0 join the queue.
If a cycle exists, its courses never reach in-degree 0.
pitfalls: Getting the edge direction backwards: [a, b] means b must come before a.
DFS cycle detection needs three colours (unvisited, in progress, done); two aren't enough.

title: Number of Provinces
summary: Count connected groups of cities from an adjacency matrix. Start with every city as its own group; union the two groups of every connected pair. Each successful union merges two groups, so the answer is n minus the number of successful unions.

complexity.note: The matrix has n² entries; union-find operations are nearly O(1).

intuition: `parent[i]` points toward the representative (root) of i's group.
find() follows parents to the root, compressing the path as it goes.
union() links one root under the other if they differ.
DFS over the matrix counting components works equally well.
pitfalls: Forgetting path compression makes find() slow on long chains.
Counting roots without calling find() on each node first.

title: Find Eventual Safe States
summary: A node is safe if every path from it ends at a terminal node (no outgoing edges). Reverse the edges and run Kahn's algorithm from the terminal nodes: a node becomes safe once all of its outgoing edges lead to safe nodes.

complexity.note: Building the reverse graph and the BFS are both linear.

intuition: Terminal nodes are safe by definition.
Count each node's outgoing edges (its out-degree).
When a safe node is confirmed, every node pointing to it loses one unresolved edge.
A node whose count hits 0 is safe; nodes on or leading into cycles never get there.
pitfalls: DFS with colouring also works; recursion depth can be an issue on long chains.

edgeCases.name: Everything is a cycle
edgeCases.why: No terminal nodes to start from.

title: Redundant Connection
summary: A tree had one extra edge added, creating exactly one cycle. Add edges one by one with union-find; the first edge whose two endpoints are already connected closes the cycle and is the answer.
intuition: Two nodes already in the same set are connected by some path.
Adding an edge between them creates a cycle.
Processing edges in order returns the last such edge in the input, as required, because there's exactly one.
pitfalls: Nodes are 1-indexed; size parent as n + 1.
DFS for every edge is O(n²).

title: Word Ladder
summary: Find the fewest words to go from `beginWord` to `endWord`, changing one letter at a time, using only words in the list. Each word is a node; BFS from the start finds the shortest path. Neighbours come from trying all 26 letters at every position.

complexity.note: N words of length L; each word generates L·26 candidates.

intuition: Shortest number of steps in an unweighted graph = BFS.
Generate neighbours by mutating one letter instead of comparing every pair of words.
Remove words from the set when queued so they're never visited twice.
The answer counts words, so the start is level 1.
pitfalls: Forgetting that endWord must be in the list.
Comparing every pair of words to build the graph is O(N²·L).
Off-by-one: the count includes both the first and last word.
